title: Feature asks heatmap + annotated synthesis (Mar 2028)
body:
Purpose:
This is a compact synthesis + annotated heatmap of customer feature asks we collected between Jan 2028 - Mar 2028 across CS calls, onboarding surveys, and field notes. The objective: give ENG/Product decision-makers a prioritized, product-lever-centric view that ties asks to actionable implementation candidates (routing, batching/cache, model variants, console UX).

Quick summary (TL;DR):
- Most frequent themes: smarter routing/fallbacks (esp. multi-tenant low-latency), prefix/KV cache controls for dynamic prompt workloads, and better observability for token-level cost breakdown.
- High commercial urgency from 4 enterprise accounts (regulated finance + healthcare) for Private deployment observability and KMS/HSM audit trails.
- Several mid-market PLG customers requesting per-route soft-SLOs and quota auto-scaling suggestions (low-effort wins).

Methodology and sources (how this was made):
- Inputs: 28 CS calls, 15 support tickets tagged "performance", onboarding survey free-text (n=120), 3 solution-engineering field reports.
- Grouped asks into canonical buckets, then scored by: frequency (F), commercial impact (I), implementation risk/time (R). Heatmap mapping: color = I*F, note shows R and suggested product lever.
- This is intentionally a synthesis (working doc) — left many raw quotes inline to keep voice/context.

Annotated heatmap (textual representation):
Rows = feature area; columns = Frequency | Commercial impact | Suggested lever | Risk/LOE
1) Smart routing & graceful fallback: F=high | I=high | Lever=route-by-latency/cost + variant fallback | Risk=med (kernel selection + routing policy logic)
   - Notes: Enterprise A (fin) requires deterministic fallbacks to quantized variants when primary capacity is exhausted.
2) Prefix/KV cache controls: F=high | I=med-high | Lever=expose cache TTL/pinning + prefix-aware metrics | Risk=low-med
   - Notes: Several customers (chatbots with long histories) report cache thrash during spikes — want per-model and per-route config.
3) Token-level cost & attribution: F=med | I=high | Lever=console + API breakdown + per-token labeling | Risk=low
   - Notes: Sales/Finance use-case: show customers cost delta between batching vs streaming for large prompt workloads.
4) Per-route soft SLOs & autoscale suggestions: F=med | I=med | Lever=dedicated autoscale hints + canary policies | Risk=med
   - Notes: This is a frequent PLG ask: let product teams set soft latency targets and get suggestions for burst capacity.
5) Private/KMS audit logging enhancements: F=med | I=high (enterprise) | Lever=private control-plane + HSM/KMS hooks + exportable logs | Risk=high (security reviews)
6) Model quality regression alerts (per-prompt set): F=low-med | I=med | Lever=optimize->quality monitors & regression gates | Risk=low-med

Top 6 asks (detailed, prioritized):
1) Deterministic fallback policies for latency/capacity constraints
   - Cue: "During peak our app started getting 3s tails — the fallback to a faster quantized model changed outputs and broke validation checks." — Enterprise A (Fin)
   - Why it matters: Keeps SLAs intact while preserving predictable behavior for regulated workflows.
   - Suggested implementation: routing policy object with prioritized model list + transform mapping (post-processing to normalize tokenization differences).
   - LOE estimate: 6-8 wks engineering + compatibility tests across 3 model families.
   - Product owner: eng-serving-runtime + product-hosted-api.

2) Expose prefix/KV cache controls and observability
   - Cue: "Our assistants have context windows of 12k tokens; the platform cache seems to evict aggressively under burst which doubles cost." — Platform PM, PLG customer
   - Why: Direct cost wins and latency reduction for chat-heavy workloads.
   - Suggested: UI toggle + API params (cache_ttl, pin_prefix=[true|false], cache_metrics per-route). Add a "cache-hit-rate" metric on console.
   - LOE: 3-5 wks (low infra risk), possible UX work 1 wk.
   - Quick win: default TTL bump for existing chat routes (A/B test) and surface immediate cost delta in console.

3) Token-level cost attribution & "what-if" analysis for batching vs streaming
   - Cue: multiple finance customers want to show cost differences to internal stakeholders.
   - Why: Transparency -> easier committed spend conversations. Also sales enablement.
   - Suggested: Console view + API endpoint returning per-request token breakdown and hypothetical cost at configured batch sizes.
   - LOE: 4 wks (front-end + instrumentation).

4) Per-route soft SLOs + autoscale suggestions
   - Cue: "We want the console to tell us if switching to dedicated or enabling burst will cut 95th percentile latency by X without doubling cost."
   - Suggestion: autoscale advisor that analyzes historical latency and recommends dedicated capacity, burst settings, or batching configs.
   - LOE: 6 wks (data infra + UI).

5) Private deployment: enhanced KMS/HSM audit trails + one-click log export
   - Enterprise asks: exportable, signed audit logs for model invocations, key usage, and admin actions.
   - Risk: high because of compliance reviews and legal signoff; also requires KMS vendor integrations.
   - LOE: 8-12 wks with security sign-off.

6) Per-prompt-set quality monitoring with regression alerting
   - Cue: "We rolled a new tokenizer/quant config and our top user flows regressed; we noticed too late." — Solutions Eng
   - Suggestion: tie Optimize evals to prod routes with automatic drift/regression detection and email/Slack alerts.
   - LOE: 5-7 wks (infra + eval infra).

Representative raw quotes (keeps context):
- "The fallback produced OK text but it failed our entity matcher — it wasn't safe to auto-deploy." — Enterprise A (Fin)
- "If we can pin a long-running chat's prefix in cache we could reduce our bill by ~30% during business hours." — PLG startup
- "We need exportable signed logs for audits; our risk team won't accept CSV snapshots." — Regulated Healthcare customer

Risk flags and unknowns (explicit):
- Fallback determinism: models have different tokenization/behavior; may need post-normalization heuristics. Risk = behavioral regression.
- KMS integrations vary by customer; HSM/SaaS variations increase integration testing.
- Cache pinning could introduce stale context for multi-user systems — must design scoping rules.

Hypotheses to validate (for PM/Eng):
- H1: Exposing cache TTL + a default TTL increase will reduce token spend 10-20% for chat-heavy customers. Measure: A/B on 8 pilot routes.
- H2: Autoscale suggestions will reduce 95th p latency complaints by giving teams actionable config (not necessarily by auto-applying capacity).

Immediate next steps (recommended):
- Sprint 1 (2 wks): run a pilot to bump cache TTL on 5 high-volume chat routes and monitor cost/latency (Owner: Solutions Eng + Obs team).
- Sprint 2 (4 wks): build a minimal token-attribution API and a simple console pane (Owner: product-hosted-api + console team).
- Security track: start KMS vendor scoping and legal intake for audit log export requirements (Owner: security-and-compliance + eng-private-deployments).

Decision requests for leadership:
- Approve 2x engineer sprint focus on cache-work and token-attribution as low-LOE, high-impact items for Q2.
- Prioritize fallback policy design for Dedicated customers with SLA commitments (budget for dedicated QA cycle).

Open questions / unresolved items: 
- Should fallback policy make content-preserving transformations automatically, or should we provide an SDK/adapter pattern so customers can write their own normalization hooks?
- For cache pinning, what multi-tenant boundaries do we enforce by default? (session-only vs route-scoped)

Notes / TODOs: 
- [TODO] Add concrete metrics sample for "cache-hit-rate" and include synthetic example on Confluence page (link above).
- [TODO] Schedule 30-min sync with product-hosted-api + eng-serving-runtime this week to align on fallback constraints.

Appendix: pilot candidate routes (short list):
- enterprise-A/validation-flow (priority)
- plg-chatbot-7 (candidate for TTL bump)
- healthcare-intake-route-3 (KMS logging pilot)

Bottom line: prioritize low-LOE, high-impact telemetry + cache controls first (fast customer wins), while scoping an enterprise-grade fallback/KMS program in parallel. This doc is a working artifact — will iterate after the 3 pilot runs and the sync with eng-serving-runtime.

-- Asha
